dedupe_keys.name: texas winter storm uri february 2021 tceq after action review of public water systems and boil water notices

description: This case study is the TCEQ fact sheet that opens its after-action review of public water systems during Winter Storm Uri in February 2021, when a Texas power and cold emergency disrupted drinking water treatment and distribution. The agency oversees more than 7,000 public water systems serving about 29 million Texans, of which 4,647 are community systems. It reports that 1,985 systems, nearly 40 percent of the community systems, issued boil water notices at the peak on 19 February 2021, and 16,351,788 people were under a notice on 18 February. Of these systems 55 percent were subject to emergency power or preparedness rules and 78 percent were small systems serving under 3,300 people. Causes named include loss of power, damaged equipment, loss of pressure and dangerous road conditions. The plan lists topics such as emergency power adequacy, weatherisation design standards, chemical and fuel supply, communication paths, alternative supplies and boil water notice procedures, gathered by surveys and round tables over about 12 months from a commissioners' tasking on 3 March 2021. Coverage: one state, one event, with counts and a plan, not the final findings. Access: free PDF; the licence is not stated. Caveats: it is an initiation fact sheet, so the recommendations came later. It informs resilience and cascading failure analysis of power and water, emergency response and boil-water models, and is related to the Texas February 2021 blackout record already in the catalogue.
